findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. The guide requires `--label bug` when creating the issue. A client-repo contributor may be allowed to open a Forge issue without permission to apply labels there. GitHub requires label permission, and [GitHub CLI passes the label into the issue creation request](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cli/cli/trunk/pkg/cmd/issue/create/create.go), so the instructed submission fails before the report reaches Forge. The issue template already declares the bug label. See [GitHub's issue permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/creating-an-issue).
findings.title: Forge bug filing fails for reporters without Forge triage access

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. On Windows PowerShell 5.1, `>` writes `forge-bug.md` as UTF-16LE ([Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_character_encoding?view=powershell-5.1)). GitHub CLI reads `--body-file` as raw bytes for the issue body ([CLI source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cli/cli/trunk/pkg/cmd/issue/create/create.go)), so the submitted template text is corrupted. This is a supported path: `scripts/install-windows.ps1:38` explicitly handles PowerShell 5.1 and `:130` tells users to open PowerShell.
findings.title: Forge bug template command fails in Windows PowerShell

stop.proposed: cut the code that invites these findings; or replace the cases with one general rule; or narrow that Done when item; or make it fail closed
stop.reason: Coordinator (both Harm 2, reversible): drop --label bug (reporters may lack label rights; the bug template already labels it), and have the agent save the filled body with its own file-writing tool as UTF-8 instead of a shell redirect, so it works in every shell.

why: When a coding agent hits a Forge bug in a client repo, nothing tells it to report the bug to Forge, so the Forge team learns late and without the details needed to fix it
